The climate in Asenovgrad

Asenovgrad is about 220 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 31°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −2°C. Around 700 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in March (about 79 mm).

Asenovgrad lies where the Chepelare river leaves the Rhodopes for the Upper Thracian Plain, about 20 km south of Plovdiv. Summers are as hot as in Plovdiv, but cooler air often drifts down the mountain valley in the evening. The sunny southern slopes and mild autumns are why vines, including the Mavrud grape, have been grown around the town for centuries.
